name: Large timeline bounds preview surfaces and backup encoding while preserving every frame pixel
description: Memory-path assertions for 64-frame artwork; exact downloaded pixels and selective preview refresh are mandatory.

planSteps.description: Open an isolated 1280x900 Studio context. Wait for active restoration. Disable native file-save picking in this context. Import a valid v3 portable fixture with 64 frames, each 128x128, one visible fully opaque layer, solid red with a green 32x32 square at (32,32). Use unique frame/layer IDs. If canvas inspection or fixture import is unavailable, report BLOCKED.
Fit the artwork. Capture every RGBA byte of the imported native artwork before editing, including the green square's actual color. Save the imported fixture. Wait for confirmed saved status.
Inspect frame-thumbnail DOM canvases. Fewer than 32 surfaces are mounted. Each backing width and height is at most 24. Retained frame buttons still represent all 64 frames.
Instrument drawImage on timeline thumbnail canvases. Activate Eraser. Erase pixel (40,40) with a single real mouse stroke. Wait for its alpha to become zero.
At most four thumbnail drawImage calls occur for this single-frame edit. Every inactive frame still retains the original artwork. Native artwork dimensions remain 128x128.

Save the edited frame. Wait for confirmed saved status. Instrument native canvas toBlob in-flight calls, decrementing only inside its completion callback. Reset the peak counter. Download the project backup.

Backup preparation reaches at most two simultaneous toBlob calls when isolated from a dirty autosave. Decode all 64 downloaded layer PNGs and compare every RGBA byte against the captured imported native artwork, with only frame one's erased pixel changed. A visual-only or name-only comparison cannot pass.
Scroll the timeline until frame 64 is visible.

Frame 64 mounts its small preview. Its green square matches exact RGBA bytes captured from the imported native artwork before editing; do not assume PNG color-profile conversion is identical across browsers. Offscreen previews release their backing surfaces. No arbitrary wait or keyboard frame-selection workaround replaces the scroll check.
